name: Bulgaria: participant-facing document QC
source: https://trialagents.com/ctis/bulgaria/en/patient-facing-document-qc-checklist (reviewed 23 September 2026); population items also from the connected Bulgaria population guides
source_note: Item sources: BG-QC#n is section n of the QC checklist page; other keys as in requirements.json sources.
item_format: Each result records the item id, the outcome, a short rationale and evidence (quoted passage and source locator) or an explicit gap.

sections.title: Trial content
sections.instruction: Compare with the current protocol and safety information.

items.check: Study title, protocol number, investigational treatment and study purpose match the current protocol.
Treatment arms, randomisation and placebo descriptions match the protocol, and the chance of being assigned to each treatment is explained.
Visit schedule and participant procedures are described accurately at a level a participant can understand.
Invasive procedures, optional procedures and remote or digital activities match the current protocol.
Expected duration of participation and any follow-up period are stated and correct.
The approximate participant number, where it appears, is correct.
Foreseeable risks and inconveniences reflect the current safety information and protocol procedures, including risks to an embryo, fetus or nursing infant where relevant.
If direct clinical benefit is not expected, this is stated clearly rather than implied.

The document states that the activity is research, the participant's responsibilities, which aspects are experimental, the available alternatives with their important risks and benefits, compensation or treatment for trial-related injury, planned payment or reimbursement, expected costs, voluntariness and the right to refuse or withdraw, new information that may affect willingness to continue, and foreseeable reasons participation may end.
Contacts are given for trial information, participant rights and trial-related injury.
Every participant procedure in the PIS matches the protocol schedule of activities.
Optional procedures are not described as mandatory participation requirements.
Contraception, pregnancy testing and pregnancy follow-up wording matches the protocol.
Biological sample types, volumes, purposes, storage and future-use statements match the protocol and sample plan.
Reimbursement and payment descriptions agree with the financial-arrangements documents (BG-P1, BG-P2).
Trial-related injury and insurance wording agrees with the Bulgaria insurance documents (BG-O1).
Withdrawal language does not promise destruction of data or samples where the protocol or applicable law provides otherwise.
Local and emergency contacts are current and suitable for Bulgaria.
The standard adult pathway requires written informed consent before enrolment, unless the protocol lawfully uses the Article 35 emergency exception.
The participant or legally designated representative and the person conducting the consent interview have the correct signature and date fields.
No witness signature is added to every ICF; witness fields appear only where the witness pathway is triggered.
Optional choices are distinguishable from the main decision; refusing optional future data or sample use is not treated as refusing the main study.
Enough time and opportunity to discuss the trial and decide is described; the participant or representative receives a copy of the signed and dated form and the written information.

sections.title: Population and document coverage
sections.instruction: Compare the protocol population with the actual document set.

items.check: Every inclusion pathway in the protocol maps to a population, populations are mutually exclusive within each consent stage, and every population has its full document set (main, representative, age-adapted, re-consent and other templates that apply), each in Bulgarian with the Bulgaria English version.

Healthy volunteers: no implied therapeutic need or expected treatment benefit; whether any direct benefit is expected is stated; confinement, fasting, dosing, sampling, restrictions and follow-up are explained; payment or reimbursement wording agrees with the Part II financial arrangements, its link to visits, time, inconvenience or expenses and the early-withdrawal rule are clear; payment is not presented as a benefit of the product.

Minors under 14: written consent of both parents or the guardians; age-appropriate information given by a physician experienced with children and adolescents; the child's refusal or wish to withdraw is taken into account; the child's form is not presented as a legal consent.

Minors 14 to 17: the ICF contains a signature field for the minor's own written informed consent (not only an assent line), plus fields for both parents or the custodian; the single-parent exception is identifiable and limited to the Article 97 cases.

Minors: re-consent at 18 is planned for participants who can reach 18 during the trial, and a participant reaching 14 gives their own written consent before continuing; no single generic minor form hides which signatures apply to which age group.

Adults who cannot legally consent: legal representative document (Article 96, or court-appointed person under Article 162(3) of the Health Act), participant information adapted to the person's understanding, participant signature and date where able, objection or dissent wording, and re-consent if capacity returns; incapacity not inferred from a diagnosis alone.

Emergency enrolment: the Article 35 conditions are reflected; consent sought without undue delay after the first intervention; what has already happened is separated from what continues only with consent; the right to object to use of data obtained is stated; no retrospective consent date.

Participant or legal representative who cannot read, or participant who cannot write: an independent witness pathway with a witness attestation stating what the witness confirms (present, information read and explained, decision freely given), the interviewer's signature kept, and the alternative means of recording described.

Pregnancy follow-up: whether the main consent already covers it is checked; a pregnant partner has a separate information and consent process; infant data, record access and follow-up duration are stated.
The participant-facing privacy explanation is consistent with the sponsor's GDPR compliance declaration (BG-R1).
Who handles trial data and the practical categories of recipients are explained where needed.
Access to source medical records by authorised monitors, auditors, ethics reviewers and regulators is described consistently with Good Clinical Practice, with confidentiality protections.
Trial-participation consent is not presented as the only possible GDPR legal basis for all trial data processing.
International transfers and central laboratories match the protocol and privacy documentation.
Withdrawal language distinguishes stopping participation from the handling of data already lawfully collected.
The PIS and ICF state the purpose, sample type, storage and relevant transfer or future-use conditions, and what happens to remaining material.
The Part II sample-compliance declaration (BG-S1) is in the package and consistent with the participant documents.
Optional future research has a separate optional choice or clearly separated consent section (separate signature or tick box); refusal does not affect main participation.

Future-use information states that the use is outside the protocol, its scope, data or sample categories, coding or anonymisation, recipients, transfers, retention, genetic or biomarker analysis where relevant, and how to withdraw; withdrawal limits after anonymisation or use match the actual sample and data plan.
Protocol-required analysis is not labelled as optional secondary use.
Bulgarian PIS and ICF present.
Corresponding Bulgaria English version present.
Recruitment arrangements and advertisements are in Bulgarian.
Participant compensation wording is consistent with the Part II financial-arrangements information.
Insurance wording is consistent with the current Bulgaria insurance documentation.
Minor consent logic matches Article 97 of the Medicinal Products in Human Medicine Act.
Site and participant numbers agree across CTIS, the site list (BG-N2) and the insurance documentation.
The current EudraLex recruitment and informed-consent procedure template v2.0 is used where applicable (new Part II submissions from 1 September 2026).
Document title, version and date are on every patient-facing document.
Bulgarian and English Bulgaria versions identify the same content version.
Signature blocks match the population and consent pathway.
Documents uploaded for review contain no completed participant signatures.
The final site-use document matches the version authorised through CTIS.
Substantial modifications: clean and tracked-change versions controlled in line with the BDA's national instructions.
Correct CTIS section and naming convention (_BG_bg and _BG_en).

No drafting instruction remains in the final version ('Инструкция за автора' paragraphs, 'Условен блок' labels, [bracket] notes, examples, unselected alternatives, yellow [INSERT/IF/CHOOSE/NOTE] labels); underscore fields completed by hand at consent stay blank.

sections.title: Readability and document design
sections.instruction: Read the Bulgarian text as a participant document, not as a protocol translation (Ordinance No 31: free of medical jargon and sufficiently understandable).

items.check: Medical and regulatory terms are defined when they cannot be avoided.
Sentences are short and wording is direct.
Main-study requirements are separated from optional choices.
Headings help a participant find risks, visits, alternatives, withdrawal, contacts and compensation.
No dense blocks copied from the protocol.
Translated terminology is consistent throughout the PIS, ICF and supporting materials, in both language versions.
The participant document list matches the protocol's populations and consent pathways and the Bulgaria Part II package checklist.
